Zarki New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Żarki, Poland

Not demolished. This cemetery, established in 1821, was enlarged several times and is now one of the largest Jewish cemeteries in the region, with about 1,100 surviving tombstones. During the October 1942 liquidation of the Żarki ghetto, the Germans shot about 300 Jews at the cemetery. Restoration work in 1983–85 was financed by Eli Zborowski, a former Żarki resident who became president of the American and International Societies for Yad Vashem. In August 2014, a set of rare cast-iron matzevot from 1880, 1886, and 1894 — found by accident in 2013 during earthworks near a nearby sanctuary — were returned to the cemetery through the efforts of local historian Wojciech Mszyca; such surviving cast-iron matzevot exist in only five or six places across all of Europe.
